rendered: The collection doesn't give a measured maximum Poisson's ratio for V2O5. The only document that discusses it, 'Tunable Mechanochemistry of Lithium Battery', says that most oxides have a Poisson coefficient “v” between 0 and 0.5[1]. That puts the upper limit at 0.5[2], but this is a general range for oxides, not a value specific to V2O5. For their V2O5 films, the authors simply assumed a Poisson coefficient v = 0.3[3] (typical for metal oxides)[4]. They used that value to estimate the in-plane strain on the film, and it is the same value used in the caption of Fig. 5[5].
